title: What happens to a plastic bottle after you recycle it?
sources: EPA Municipal Solid Waste Recycling Report

lines.text: When you toss a plastic water bottle into the blue recycling bin, where does it actually go?
A collection truck transports it to a Materials Recovery Facility packed with robotic conveyor belts.
Optical infrared scanners shoot light beams through the plastics, identifying PET plastic in milliseconds.
High-pressure air jets shoot the bottle into designated bins, where it gets crushed into giant cubes.
lines.caps: Air jets blast the *bottle | into designated *bales

lines.text: The bales are shredded into microscopic plastic flakes, washed in hot caustic baths, and melted into pellets.
lines.caps: Shredded into *flakes | and melted into plastic *pellets

lines.text: Those pellets get spun into polyester yarn for fleece jackets, carpets, or molded into brand new bottles.
lines.caps: Spun into fleece *jackets | or molded into new *bottles!

lines.text: Recycling a single bottle saves enough energy to power a laptop for three straight hours.
lines.caps: One recycled bottle *powers | a laptop for *3 hours!
